items.en: I finished the work in two hours.
items.notes: « en » measures how long a task takes, while « dans » points to when it will happen.

items.fr: On peut y aller en vingt minutes à pied.
items.en: We can get there in twenty minutes on foot.

items.fr: Il a appris à conduire en un mois.
items.en: He learned to drive in a month.

items.fr: Elle a lu le livre en trois jours.
items.en: She read the book in three days.

items.fr: En combien de temps peux-tu être prêt ?
items.en: How quickly can you be ready?

items.fr: Le gâteau cuit en quarante minutes.
items.en: The cake bakes in forty minutes.

items.fr: En une semaine, tout était réglé.
items.en: In one week, everything was settled.

items.fr: J'ai pris rendez-vous chez le médecin.
items.en: I made an appointment with the doctor.

items.fr: Notre rendez-vous est fixé à quinze heures.
items.en: Our appointment is set for three PM.

items.fr: Je dois reporter le rendez-vous à demain.
items.en: I have to postpone the appointment until tomorrow.

items.fr: Le rendez-vous a été confirmé par courriel.
items.en: The appointment was confirmed by email.

items.fr: N'oublie pas ton rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
Le train a dix minutes de retard.
items.en: The train is ten minutes late.

items.fr: Désolé, je vais être en retard de vingt minutes.
items.en: Sorry, I'm going to be twenty minutes late.

items.fr: Il arrive toujours en retard aux réunions.
items.en: He always arrives late to meetings.

items.fr: Nous sommes en retard sur le planning.
Ne sois pas en retard, s'il te plaît.
Elle est arrivée en retard à cause de la circulation.
items.en: She arrived late because of traffic.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux arriver un peu en avance.
items.en: It's better to arrive a bit early.

items.fr: Je suis arrivé dix minutes en avance.
Le projet est en avance sur le calendrier.
items.en: The project is ahead of schedule.

items.fr: Elle est toujours en avance, jamais en retard.
On peut arriver une demi-heure en avance si tu veux.
items.en: We can arrive half an hour early if you want.

items.fr: Le vol est arrivé à l'heure prévue.
items.en: The flight arrived at the scheduled time.

items.fr: Essaie d'être à l'heure demain matin.
items.en: Try to be on time tomorrow morning.

items.fr: Le cours commence toujours à l'heure pile.
items.en: The class always starts right on time.
Thank you for arriving on time.

items.fr: Le bus est rarement à l'heure ici.
items.en: The bus is rarely on time here.
Let's hurry, the movie is about to start.

items.fr: Il faut se dépêcher pour ne pas rater le train.
items.en: We need to hurry so we don't miss the train.

items.fr: Dépêche-toi un peu, on va être en retard.
items.en: Hurry up a little, we're going to be late.

items.fr: Elle s'est dépêchée pour arriver avant midi.
items.en: She hurried to arrive before noon.

items.fr: Pas la peine de se dépêcher, on a le temps.
items.en: No need to hurry, we have time.

items.fr: Dépêchez-vous, la réunion commence dans cinq minutes.
items.en: Hurry up, the meeting starts in five minutes.

items.fr: La semaine prochaine, je pars en vacances.
items.en: Next week, I'm going on vacation.

items.fr: La semaine dernière a été très chargée.
On se revoit la semaine prochaine, alors.
La semaine dernière, il a fait très froid.
items.en: Last week, it was very cold.

items.fr: Le mois dernier, j'ai commencé un nouveau travail.
items.en: Last month, I started a new job.

items.fr: Le mois prochain marque mon premier anniversaire ici.
items.en: Next month marks my first anniversary here.

items.fr: Le mois dernier est passé très vite.
items.en: Last month went by very quickly.

items.fr: L'année dernière, nous avons visité le Portugal.
L'année prochaine sera pleine de projets.
items.en: Next year will be full of projects.

items.fr: L'année dernière à la même époque, il neigeait.
items.en: Last year at this time, it was snowing.

items.fr: Chaque jour, je révise un peu de vocabulaire.
items.en: Every day, I review a bit of vocabulary.

items.fr: Chaque semaine, on fait les courses ensemble.
items.en: Every week, we do the shopping together.

items.fr: Chaque mois, elle met un peu d'argent de côté.
items.en: Every month, she puts a little money aside.

items.fr: Tous les jours, il se lève à six heures.
items.en: Every day, he gets up at six o'clock.

items.fr: Tous les mois, la facture arrive le même jour.
items.en: Every month, the bill arrives on the same day.

items.fr: Tous les week-ends, on va à la campagne.
items.en: Every weekend, we go to the countryside.

items.fr: Le temps presse, il faut se décider.
items.en: Time is pressing, we need to decide.

items.fr: Il était temps que tu arrives !
Prends ton temps, rien ne presse.
items.en: Take your time, there's no rush.

items.fr: Elle a pris tout son temps pour répondre.
items.en: She took her sweet time to answer.

items.fr: Il ne faut pas perdre de temps.
Ça permettra de gagner du temps.
Au fil du temps, on s'habitue à tout.
items.en: Over time, you get used to everything.

items.fr: À la longue, ça devient plus facile.
items.en: In the long run, it becomes easier.

items.fr: Sur le long terme, ce choix est le bon.
items.en: In the long term, this choice is the right one.

items.fr: D'un jour à l'autre, tout peut changer.
items.en: From one day to the next, everything can change.

items.fr: Il vit au jour le jour, sans vraiment planifier.
items.en: He lives day to day, without really planning.

items.fr: Du jour au lendemain, elle a changé de vie.
En temps voulu, tu sauras tout.
items.en: In due time, you'll know everything.

items.fr: Il faut agir en temps et en heure.
items.en: We need to act at the right time.

items.fr: Avant qu'il ne soit trop tard, parle-lui.
items.en: Before it's too late, talk to her.

items.fr: Il est grand temps de faire une pause.
items.en: It's high time we took a break.

items.fr: Ça fait une éternité qu'on n'a pas dîné ensemble.
items.en: It's been ages since we had dinner together.

items.fr: Le temps file à une vitesse folle.
items.en: Time flies at an incredible speed.

items.fr: Les jours se suivent et ne se ressemblent pas ici.
items.notes: A play on the classic idiom « les jours se suivent et se ressemblent », which usually describes monotony.

items.fr: Rome ne s'est pas faite en un jour.
items.en: Rome wasn't built in a day.

items.fr: Demain, il sera trop tard pour changer d'avis.
items.en: Tomorrow, it will be too late to change your mind.

items.fr: On verra bien ce que l'avenir nous réserve.
items.en: We'll see what the future holds for us.

example.en: The living room clock runs a bit fast.
example.fr: La pendule du salon avance un peu.

example.en: The clock face is a bit dirty.
example.fr: Le cadran de l'horloge est un peu sale.

example.en: The hour hand is pointing at three.
example.fr: L'aiguille des heures pointe vers le trois.

example.en: I set the timer for ten minutes.
example.fr: J'ai réglé le minuteur sur dix minutes.

example.en: The second hand goes around the clock face in one minute.
example.fr: La trotteuse fait le tour du cadran en une minute.

items.fr: Mon frère a vingt et un ans.
items.en: My brother is twenty-one years old.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a vɛ̃ e œ̃ nɑ̃
items.notes: "Vingt et un" always uses "et", never a hyphen before "un".

items.en: She is eighty-one years old today.
items.ipa: ɛl a ka.tʁə.vɛ̃ œ̃ ɑ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: "Quatre-vingt-un" loses the s because a number follows "quatre-vingt".

items.fr: Il habite au numéro quarante-sept de la rue.
items.en: He lives at number forty-seven on the street.
items.ipa: il a.bit o ny.me.ʁo ka.ʁɑ̃t sɛt də la ʁy
items.notes: Compound numbers below one hundred take hyphens between their parts, except around "et".

items.fr: Nous avons réservé une table pour six personnes.
items.en: We reserved a table for six people.
items.ipa: nu.z a.vɔ̃ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl puʁ si pɛʁ.sɔn
items.notes: "Six" loses its final consonant sound before "personnes".

items.fr: Mon grand-père est né en dix-neuf cent trente-huit.
items.en: My grandfather was born in nineteen thirty-eight.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ pɛʁ ɛ ne ɑ̃ diz.nœf sɑ̃ tʁɑ̃t ɥit
items.notes: Compound numbers below one hundred take hyphens between their parts, except around "et".

items.fr: Mon salaire mensuel est de deux mille cinq cents euros.
items.en: My monthly salary is two thousand five hundred euros.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ sa.lɛʁ mɑ̃.sɥɛl ɛ də dø mil sɛ̃k sɑ̃.z ø.ʁo
items.notes: "Mille" is always invariable, it never takes an s.

items.fr: Il y a cent chances sur cent qu'il pleuve demain.
items.en: There is a hundred percent chance it will rain tomorrow.
items.ipa: il i a sɑ̃ ʃɑ̃s syʁ sɑ̃ kil plœv də.mɛ̃
items.notes: "Cent" sounds exactly like "sang" and "sans" but is spelled differently.

items.fr: Mon oncle a passé quarante ans dans la même maison.
items.en: My uncle spent forty years in the same house.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n ɔ̃kl a pa.se ka.ʁɑ̃t ɑ̃ dɑ̃ la mɛm mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: The number liaises with the following vowel-initial word, adding a consonant sound that is not written.

items.fr: Pour la cuisine, nous avons acheté six chaises et une table.
items.en: For the kitchen, we bought six chairs and a table.
items.ipa: puʁ la kɥi.zin nu.z a.vɔ̃ aʃ.te si ʃɛz e yn tabl
items.notes: "Six" loses its final consonant sound before "chaises".

items.fr: Le concert a attiré plus de cinquante mille spectateurs.
items.en: The concert attracted more than fifty thousand spectators.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ a a.ti.ʁe plys də sɛ̃.kɑ̃t mil spɛk.ta.tœʁ
items.notes: "Mille" is always invariable, it never takes an s.

items.fr: Après deux mille sept, la ville a doublé sa population.
items.en: After two thousand seven, the town's population doubled.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ dø mil sɛt la vil a du.ble sa pɔ.py.la.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "Mille" is always invariable, it never takes an s.

items.fr: Ce moulin fonctionne encore après plus de quatre cents ans.
items.en: This mill still runs after more than four hundred years.
items.ipa: sə mu.lɛ̃ fɔ̃k.sjɔn ɑ̃.kɔʁ a.pʁɛ plys də ka.tʁə sɑ̃.z ɑ̃
items.notes: "Cent" takes an s here as a round multiple of a hundred with no smaller number following.

items.fr: La montagne culmine à quatre mille huit cent dix mètres.
items.en: The mountain peaks at four thousand eight hundred ten meters.
items.ipa: la mɔ̃.taɲ kyl.min a katʁ mil ɥi sɑ̃ dis mɛtʁ
items.notes: "Mille" is always invariable, it never takes an s.

items.fr: Pour la fête, nous avons besoin de cent cinquante chaises.
items.en: For the party, we need one hundred fifty chairs.
items.ipa: puʁ la fɛt nu.z a.vɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃ də sɑ̃ sɛ̃.kɑ̃t ʃɛz
items.notes: "Cent" is invariable here since it is not a round multiple of a hundred used alone.

items.fr: Trois cents chaises supplémentaires sont encore nécessaires.
items.en: Three hundred extra chairs are still needed.
items.ipa: tʁwa sɑ̃ ʃɛz sy.ple.mɑ̃.tɛʁ sɔ̃.t ɑ̃.kɔʁ ne.se.sɛʁ

items.fr: Depuis quarante ans, ce professeur enseigne dans la même école.
items.en: For forty years, this teacher has taught at the same school.
items.ipa: də.pɥi ka.ʁɑ̃t ɑ̃ sə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ ɑ̃.sɛɲ dɑ̃ la mɛm e.kɔl

items.fr: Ce camion a parcouru plus de deux cent mille kilomètres.
items.en: This truck has traveled more than two hundred thousand kilometers.
items.ipa: sə ka.mjɔ̃ a paʁ.ku.ʁy plys də dø sɑ̃ mil ki.lɔ.mɛtʁ
items.notes: "Mille" is always invariable, it never takes an s.

items.fr: En une seule journée, nous avons parcouru cent quatre-vingts kilomètres.
items.en: In a single day, we covered one hundred eighty kilometers.
items.ipa: ɑ̃.n yn sœl ʒuʁ.ne nu.z a.vɔ̃ paʁ.ku.ʁy sɑ̃ ka.tʁə.vɛ̃ ki.lɔ.mɛtʁ
items.notes: "Quatre-vingts" keeps the s because no smaller number follows within the compound.

items.fr: Ce soir, le ciel comptait plus de cent étoiles visibles.
items.en: Tonight, the sky held more than a hundred visible stars.
items.ipa: sə swaʁ lə sjɛl kɔ̃.tɛ plys də sɑ̃.t e.twal vi.zibl
items.notes: The number liaises with the following vowel-initial word, adding a consonant sound that is not written.

items.fr: En cinquante ans, ce médecin a soigné des milliers de patients.
items.en: Over fifty years, this doctor treated thousands of patients.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ sɛ̃.kɑ̃t ɑ̃ sə med.sɛ̃ a swa.ɲe de mi.lje də pa.sjɑ̃

items.fr: Ce forgeron travaille le métal depuis soixante ans.
items.en: This blacksmith has worked metal for sixty years.
items.ipa: sə fɔʁ.ʒə.ʁɔ̃ tʁa.vaj lə me.tal də.pɥi swa.sɑ̃.t ɑ̃
items.notes: The number liaises with the following vowel-initial word, adding a consonant sound that is not written.

items.fr: Le dimanche soir, je prépare mes affaires pour la semaine.
items.en: On Sunday evenings, I get my things ready for the week.
items.ipa: lə di.mɑ̃ʃ swaʁ ʒə pʁe.paʁ me za.fɛʁ puʁ la sə.mɛn
items.notes: 'Le dimanche soir' describes a weekly ritual, not just one particular Sunday.

items.fr: Nous nous marions en septembre prochain.
items.ipa: nu nu ma.ʁjɔ̃ ɑ̃ sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃

items.fr: Le premier avril, on fait des blagues.
items.en: On the first of April, people play pranks.
items.ipa: lə pʁə.mje a.vʁil ɔ̃ fɛ de blag

items.notes: "Marron" comes from the fruit name and never agrees, even in the plural.

items.fr: Le salon du livre a lieu chaque octobre.
items.en: The book fair takes place every October.
items.ipa: lə sa.lɔ̃ dy livʁ a ljø ʃak ɔk.tɔbʁ

items.fr: En novembre, on pense déjà aux fêtes de fin d'année.
items.en: In November, people already think about the end-of-year holidays.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ ɔ̃ pɑ̃s de.ʒa o fɛt də fɛ̃ da.ne
items.notes: Month names like 'novembre' are never capitalized unless they open the sentence.

items.fr: Mon anniversaire est le quatorze juillet, le jour de la fête nationale.
items.en: My birthday is on July fourteenth, Bastille Day.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ na.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ ɛ lə ka.tɔʁz ʒɥi.jɛ lə ʒuʁ də la fɛt na.sjɔ.nal
items.notes: Even in a fixed expression like 'la fête nationale', the month 'juillet' stays lowercase.

items.fr: Ce mois-ci, c'est moi qui organise la fête d'anniversaire.
items.en: This month, it's me who's organizing the birthday party.
items.ipa: sə mwa.si sɛ mwa ki ɔʁ.ga.niz la fɛt da.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: 'Mois' (month) and 'moi' (me) are pronounced exactly the same, only the spelling differs.

items.fr: Mon fils aura sept ans en mars prochain.
items.en: My son will turn seven next March.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis o.ʁa sɛ.t ɑ̃ ɑ̃ maʁs pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: Even with 'prochain' right after it, 'mars' is not capitalized.

items.fr: L'invitation précise que la fête commence samedi à dix-huit heures.
items.en: The invitation says the party starts Saturday at six p.m.
items.ipa: lɛ̃.vi.ta.sjɔ̃ pʁe.siz kə la fɛt kɔ.mɑ̃s sam.di a di.zɥi.t œʁ

items.fr: L'Épiphanie se célèbre début janvier avec une galette.
items.en: Epiphany is celebrated in early January with a special cake.
items.ipa: le.pi.fa.ni sə se.lɛbʁ de.by ʒɑ̃.vje a.vɛk yn ga.lɛt

items.fr: En décembre, la ville est décorée de guirlandes lumineuses.
items.en: In December, the city is decorated with light garlands.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ la vil ɛ de.kɔ.ʁe də giʁ.lɑ̃d ly.mi.nøz
items.notes: 'Décembre' keeps its accent aigu on the é.

items.fr: Le facteur ne passe jamais le dimanche.
items.en: The mailman never comes on Sundays.
items.ipa: lə fak.tœʁ nə pas ʒa.mɛ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: 'Le dimanche' here means every Sunday, never just one.

items.fr: La Révolution française a commencé en juillet mille sept cent quatre-vingt-neuf.
items.en: The French Revolution began in July seventeen eighty-nine.
items.ipa: la ʁe.vɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ fʁɑ̃.sɛz a kɔ.mɑ̃.se ɑ̃ ʒɥi.jɛ mil sɛt sɑ̃ ka.tʁə.vɛ̃.nœf

items.fr: En France, le onze novembre commémore la fin de la Première Guerre mondiale.
items.en: In France, November eleventh commemorates the end of World War One.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s lə ɔ̃z nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ kɔ.me.mɔʁ la fɛ̃ də la pʁə.mjɛʁ gɛʁ mɔ̃.djal
items.notes: 'Novembre' stays lowercase even though 'onze novembre' names a famous historical date.

items.fr: Elle a une nouvelle voiture rouge.
items.en: She has a new red car.
items.ipa: ɛl a yn nu.vɛl vwa.tyʁ ʁuʒ
items.notes: 'Nouveau' becomes 'nouvelle' in the feminine.

items.respell: puh-ZAY lay lay-güm ah-vahn duh peh-YAY

items.fr: arriver tôt pour éviter la foule
items.en: to arrive early to avoid the crowd
items.respell: ah-ree-VAY toh poor ay-vee-TAY lah FOOL

items.en: to take advantage of low prices
to ask for a paper bag
to give change to the customer

items.fr: flâner entre les étals du marché
items.en: to stroll between the market stalls
items.respell: flah-NAY ahntr lay zay-tal dü mar-SHAY

items.en: a slice of bread with topping
a Viennese hot chocolate (with whipped cream)
a croque-monsieur (grilled ham and cheese sandwich)

items.respell: ehs kuh lah TAHBL eh LEE-bruh

items.fr: Je voudrais un café avec du lait.
items.en: I would like a coffee with milk.

to be used to doing something
to get into the habit of

to get away, to escape from routine

items.fr: Ils vont bientôt fermer le café.
items.en: They are going to close the café soon.
items.notes: Fermer ends in a silent r, so it sounds the same as fermé.
The final ds in prends is silent, so prends and prend sound identical.

items.en: She is drinking a hot chocolate.
items.notes: The final t of chocolat and the final d of chaud are both silent.

items.fr: Nous allons au café ce matin.
items.en: We are going to the café this morning.
items.notes: Nous allons requires a liaison, so the silent s links to the next vowel as a z sound.

items.en: They are arriving at the terrace.
items.notes: The liaison between ils and arrivent turns the silent s into a z sound.
The final d in chaud is never pronounced.

items.en: The customers are waiting for their order.
items.notes: The verb ending ent in attendent is completely silent.

items.fr: Elle prend un thé avec du citron.
items.en: She is having a tea with lemon.
items.ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ œ̃ te a.vɛk dy si.tʁɔ̃/
items.notes: The final d of prend is silent, just like in the form prends.
The final s of croissants is silent even though the word is plural.

items.fr: Nous partageons une tarte aux pommes.
items.en: We are sharing an apple tart.
items.notes: The ending ons in partageons keeps a nasal sound, not two separate letters.
The final s of serveurs and of gentils both stay silent.

items.en: She is asking the waiter for the bill.
items.notes: La becomes l' before addition since the word starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Il boit son café sans sucre.
items.en: He drinks his coffee without sugar.
items.notes: Son and sans share a similar nasal sound but are spelled very differently.
Elles commandent sounds identical to elle commande despite the plural subject.
The final s of verres is silent even though it marks the plural.

items.fr: Nous choisissons une table en terrasse.
items.en: We are choosing a table on the terrace.
items.notes: The ending ons in choisissons keeps one nasal sound, not two separate letters.

items.fr: Il paie l'addition tout de suite.
items.en: He pays the bill right away.
items.notes: Paie is pronounced like pè, the final e stays silent.

items.fr: Elle aime le café au lait.
items.notes: Aime ends in a silent e that is never pronounced.

items.fr: Les tasses sont sur la table.
items.en: The cups are on the table.
items.notes: The final s of tasses stays silent even though it shows the plural.

items.fr: Il retrouve ses amis au café.
items.en: He is meeting his friends at the café.
items.notes: Ses amis needs a liaison, so the silent s becomes a z sound.

items.fr: Elle prend deux sucres dans son café.
items.en: She takes two sugars in her coffee.
items.ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ dø sykʁ dɑ̃ sɔ̃ ka.fe/
items.notes: Deux ends with a silent x that is never heard.

items.en: We each pay our own share.
items.notes: Payons keeps the nasal on sound spelled with the letters ons.

items.fr: Ils préfèrent la salle plutôt que la terrasse.
items.en: They prefer the indoor room rather than the terrace.
items.ipa: /il pʁe.fɛʁ la sal ply.to kə la tɛ.ʁas/
items.notes: Préfèrent ends in a silent ent, sounding just like the singular préfère.
Le becomes l' before addition since the word starts with a vowel sound.
The final t of petit is silent before a consonant sound.
Restons assis needs a liaison, so the silent s links as a z sound.

items.fr: Il boit son café d'un trait.
items.en: He drinks his coffee in one gulp.
items.notes: D'un links de and un together, dropping the vowel of de.
Sont encore takes a liaison, so the normally silent t is pronounced.

items.fr: Elle commande la même chose que lui.
items.en: She orders the same thing as him.
items.ipa: /ɛl kɔ.mɑ̃d la mɛm ʃoz kə lɥi/
items.notes: Même ends in a silent e that simply softens the m sound.

items.fr: Ils partagent l'addition à la fin.
items.en: They split the bill at the end.
items.notes: L' replaces la before addition because the word begins with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle a commandé un café crème.
items.en: She ordered a coffee with milk.
items.notes: Commandé, commander and commandez all sound the same; only spelling shows the tense.

items.en: We are going to have a dessert.
items.notes: Allons needs a liaison, so the silent s links to the next vowel.

items.fr: Il a payé l'addition avant de partir.
items.en: He paid the bill before leaving.
items.ipa: /il a pɛ.je la.di.sjɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/
items.notes: Payé sounds exactly like payer and payez, even though the tense differs.

items.fr: Nous avons laissé un bon pourboire.
items.notes: Laissé sounds identical to laisser, even though the tense is different.

items.en: She is going to order a salad.
items.notes: Commander ends in a silent r, so it sounds just like commandé.

items.fr: Ils ont pris leurs cafés à emporter.
items.en: They took their coffees to go.
items.notes: Ont and on sound identical, but only ont means they have.

items.fr: On a réservé une table en terrasse.
items.en: We reserved a table on the terrace.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ a ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl ɑ̃ tɛ.ʁas/
items.notes: On is pronounced exactly like ont, so context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Elle est allée au café avec sa sœur.
items.en: She went to the café with her sister.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le o ka.fe a.vɛk sa sœʁ/
items.notes: Allée takes an extra silent e to agree with the feminine subject elle.

items.fr: Nous avons trouvé la tarte délicieuse.
items.notes: Trouvé stays masculine here because the direct object comes after the verb.

items.fr: Les cafés qu'elle a commandés étaient froids.
items.en: The coffees she ordered were cold.
items.ipa: /le ka.fe kɛl a kɔ.mɑ̃.de e.tɛ fʁwa/
items.notes: Commandés adds a silent s to agree with cafés, placed before the verb.

items.fr: Il va payer l'addition tout à l'heure.
items.en: He is going to pay the bill in a moment.
items.notes: À in tout à l'heure needs its accent, unlike the verb form a.

items.fr: Nous avons discuté ou nous avons juste bu un café.
items.en: We chatted, or we just had a coffee.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dis.ky.te u nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʒyst by œ̃ ka.fe/
items.notes: Ou without an accent means or, while où with an accent means where.

items.fr: Elle a demandé où se trouvaient les toilettes.
items.en: She asked where the restrooms were.
items.ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de u sə tʁu.vɛ le twa.lɛt/
items.notes: Où keeps its accent because it means where, unlike the conjunction ou.

items.fr: Nous avons partagé l'addition à la fin du repas.
items.en: We split the bill at the end of the meal.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ paʁ.ta.ʒe la.di.sjɔ̃ a la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
items.notes: Partagé is distinguished from partager only by spelling, not by sound.

items.fr: Elle a acheté deux croissants qu'elle a partagés avec moi.
items.en: She bought two croissants that she shared with me.
items.ipa: /ɛl a aʃ.te dø kʁwa.sɑ̃ kɛl a paʁ.ta.ʒe a.vɛk mwa/
items.notes: Partagés takes a silent s to agree with the plural croissants placed earlier in the sentence.

items.fr: Il faut que tu viennes au café avec nous.
items.en: You need to come to the café with us.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ty vjɛn o ka.fe a.vɛk nu/
items.notes: Viennes in the subjunctive is pronounced with an audible n, unlike the indicative vient.

items.fr: Je ne pense pas qu'il finisse son café à temps.
items.en: I don't think he will finish his coffee in time.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kil fi.nis sɔ̃ ka.fe a tɑ̃/
items.notes: Finisse in the subjunctive is spelled with a double s, unlike the indicative finit.

items.fr: C'est le café où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
items.en: This is the café where we met.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə ka.fe u nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe/
items.notes: Rencontrés agrees with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s.

items.fr: Ce serveur est plus rapide que celui d'hier.
items.en: This waiter is faster than yesterday's.
items.ipa: /sə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ ply ʁa.pid kə sə.lɥi djɛʁ/
items.notes: Ce before a noun is a demonstrative, not to be confused with the pronoun se.

items.fr: Elle se demande si le café est encore ouvert.
items.en: She wonders if the café is still open.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə də.mɑ̃d si lə ka.fe ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ u.vɛʁ/
items.notes: Se before the verb is a reflexive pronoun, unlike the demonstrative ce.

items.fr: Ces cafés coûtent plus cher que ses habitudes ne le permettent.
items.en: These coffees cost more than his habits allow.
items.ipa: /se ka.fe kut ply ʃɛʁ kə se a.bi.tyd nə lə pɛʁ.mɛt/
items.notes: Ces, ses and c'est are all pronounced the same but never interchangeable in writing.

items.fr: C'est le meilleur café du quartier.
items.en: It's the best café in the neighborhood.
items.notes: C'est contracts cela est and sounds exactly like ces and ses.

items.fr: Quel café préfères-tu, celui-ci ou celui-là.
items.en: Which coffee do you prefer, this one or that one.
items.ipa: /kɛl ka.fe pʁe.fɛʁ ty sə.lɥi.si u sə.lɥi.la/
items.notes: Quel agrees with the masculine noun café, unlike the feminine form quelle.

items.en: Which terrace do you prefer in summer.
items.notes: Quelle takes the extra silent e to agree with the feminine noun terrasse.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, le café reste ouvert.
items.en: Although it is late, the café stays open.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ lə ka.fe ʁɛst u.vɛʁ/
items.notes: Soit is the subjunctive of être and must not be confused with the word soi.

items.fr: Je doute que ce serveur se souvienne de notre commande.
items.en: I doubt this waiter remembers our order.
items.ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sɛʁ.vœʁ sə su.vjɛn də nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
items.notes: Se souvienne uses the subjunctive with an audible final n, unlike se souvient.

items.fr: Les clients ont attendu longtemps avant qu'on les serve.
items.en: The customers waited a long time before they were served.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃.t‿a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ kɔ̃ le sɛʁv/
items.notes: Serve in the subjunctive drops the final t found in the indicative form sert.

items.fr: C'est la première fois qu'elle vient dans ce café.
items.en: It's the first time she has come to this café.
items.ipa: /sɛ la pʁə.mjɛʁ fwa kɛl vjɛ̃ dɑ̃ sə ka.fe/
items.notes: C'est here cannot be replaced by ses or ces, even though all three sound alike.

items.fr: Il semble que les prix aient encore augmenté.
items.en: It seems that prices have gone up again.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le pʁi ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ o.gmɑ̃.te/
items.notes: Aient, the plural subjunctive of avoir, is pronounced just like the singular ait.

items.fr: Nous aimerions nous asseoir en terrasse, si cela ne vous dérange pas.
items.en: We would like to sit on the terrace, if that doesn't bother you.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿ɛ.mə.ʁjɔ̃ nu.z‿a.swaʁ ɑ̃ tɛ.ʁas si sə.la nə vu de.ʁɑ̃ʒ pa/
items.notes: Aimerions in the conditional needs a liaison right after nous.

items.fr: Quelles que soient ses habitudes, il commande toujours la même chose.
items.en: Whatever his habits are, he always orders the same thing.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t se a.bi.tyd il kɔ.mɑ̃d tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm ʃoz/
items.notes: Ses here is a possessive pronoun, not to be confused with c'est or ces.

items.fr: Il est possible que le serveur ait oublié notre commande.
items.en: It is possible that the waiter forgot our order.
items.ipa: /il ɛ pɔ.sibl kə lə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ.t‿u.bli.je nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
items.notes: Ait, the subjunctive of avoir, sounds exactly like the noun est or the verb es.

items.fr: Bien que ce café soit cher, il reste toujours plein.
items.en: Although this café is expensive, it is always full.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə ka.fe swa ʃɛʁ il ʁɛst tu.ʒuʁ plɛ̃/
items.notes: Ce before café is the demonstrative adjective, unlike the pronoun se in reflexive verbs.

items.fr: Les touristes ne savent pas quels cafés sont les plus authentiques.
items.en: The tourists don't know which cafés are the most authentic.
items.ipa: /le tu.ʁist nə sav pa kɛl ka.fe sɔ̃ le plyz‿o.tɑ̃.tik/
items.notes: Quels agrees with the plural masculine cafés, adding a silent s.

items.fr: Il faut absolument que nous choisissions une table à l'ombre.
items.en: We absolutely need to choose a table in the shade.
items.ipa: /il fo.t‿ab.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ kə nu ʃwa.zi.sjɔ̃ yn tabl a lɔ̃bʁ/
items.notes: Choisissions in the subjunctive adds an extra syllable not heard in the indicative form.

items.fr: Il mélange la farine et les oeufs frais.
items.en: He mixes the flour and the fresh eggs.
items.ipa: /il melɑ̃ʒ la faʁin e lez‿ø fʁɛ/
items.notes: Les oeufs needs the z liaison from les even though oeufs itself starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Je coupe les oignons pour la soupe.
items.en: I cut the onions for the soup.
items.notes: The liaison between les and oignons adds a z sound that is easy to miss when writing.

items.fr: Elle épluche les carottes avec un couteau.
items.en: She peels the carrots with a knife.
items.ipa: /ɛl eplyʃ le kaʁɔt avɛk œ̃ kuto/
items.notes: The plural s on carottes is completely silent, so listen for les to know it is plural.

items.fr: Nous mangeons du pain frais chaque matin.
items.en: We eat fresh bread every morning.
items.ipa: /nu mɑ̃ʒɔ̃ dy pɛ̃ fʁɛ ʃak matɛ̃/
items.notes: Pain and matin both end in the nasal vowel in, which has no separate n sound to write out.

items.fr: Il boit un café sans sucre.
items.notes: Sans sounds exactly like sang and cent, so rely on meaning to spell it correctly.

items.fr: Tu manges une pomme à midi.
items.en: You eat an apple at noon.
items.notes: The preposition à sounds identical to the verb form a, but only one has an accent.

items.fr: Les enfants aiment les pâtes au fromage.
items.en: The children like pasta with cheese.
items.notes: Les enfants is joined by a z liaison that must not be forgotten in writing.

items.fr: Le chef prépare un plat délicieux.
items.en: The chef prepares a delicious dish.
items.notes: The final t of plat is never pronounced, which often leads learners to drop it in spelling too.

items.fr: Nous achetons des ananas au marché.
items.en: We buy pineapples at the market.
items.notes: Des ananas carries a z liaison from des that links smoothly into the vowel of ananas.

items.fr: Elle met un peu de sel dans la soupe.
items.en: She puts a little salt in the soup.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɛ œ̃ pø də sɛl dɑ̃ la sup/
items.notes: The verb met and the noun mets, meaning a dish, sound the same, so context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Il coupe le pain en tranches fines.
items.en: He cuts the bread into thin slices.
items.ipa: /il kup lə pɛ̃ ɑ̃ tʁɑ̃ʃ fin/
items.notes: En and tranches both use nasal vowels that have no audible n or m to copy down.

items.fr: Je fais cuire le riz dans l'eau chaude.
items.en: I cook the rice in hot water.
items.ipa: /ʒə fɛ kɥiʁ lə ʁi dɑ̃ lo ʃod/
items.notes: La eau is impossible to say, so la elides to l' before the vowel of eau.

items.fr: Les oeufs sont dans le réfrigérateur.
items.en: The eggs are in the refrigerator.
items.notes: Unlike singular un oeuf where the f is heard, the f and s of plural oeufs both stay silent.

items.fr: Tu bois de l'eau avec ton repas.
items.en: You drink water with your meal.
items.ipa: /ty bwa də lo avɛk tɔ̃ ʁəpa/
items.notes: De drops its e before the vowel in eau, becoming de l'eau.

items.fr: Nous préparons le dîner ensemble ce soir.
items.en: We are preparing dinner together tonight.
items.ipa: /nu pʁepaʁɔ̃ lə dine ɑ̃sɑ̃bl sə swaʁ/
items.notes: Dîner keeps a circumflex accent on the i even though it does not change the sound.

items.fr: Elle achète des fruits frais tous les jours.
items.en: She buys fresh fruit every day.
items.ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt de fʁɥi fʁɛ tu le ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before a consonant, tous drops its final s sound, unlike when it stands alone.

items.fr: Les tomates sont mûres et rouges.
items.en: The tomatoes are ripe and red.
items.notes: Sont is a homophone of son, so only the sentence meaning tells them apart.

items.fr: Je goûte la sauce avant de servir.
items.en: I taste the sauce before serving.
items.ipa: /ʒə gut la sos avɑ̃ də sɛʁviʁ/
items.notes: Goûte keeps its circumflex accent on the u, a spelling detail invisible in speech.

items.fr: Vous mangez du poulet rôti ce soir.
items.en: You are eating roast chicken tonight.
items.ipa: /vu mɑ̃ʒe dy pulɛ ʁoti sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The final t of poulet is always silent, like most words ending in -et.

items.fr: Elle lave les fraises dans l'évier.
items.en: She washes the strawberries in the sink.
items.notes: La évier cannot be said aloud, so la becomes l' before the vowel.

items.fr: Il ajoute du poivre sur la viande.
items.en: He adds pepper to the meat.
items.ipa: /il aʒut dy pwavʁ syʁ la vjɑ̃d/
items.notes: Sur, meaning on, and sûr, meaning certain, sound identical, only the accent tells them apart in writing.

items.fr: Nous cuisinons ensemble le dimanche matin.
items.en: We cook together on Sunday morning.
items.notes: Ensemble and dimanche both hide nasal vowels with no separate n or m sound.

items.fr: Ils mangent des légumes verts chaque soir.
items.en: They eat green vegetables every evening.
items.ipa: /il mɑ̃ʒ de legym vɛʁ ʃak swaʁ/
items.notes: Mangent sounds exactly like the singular mange, so only the subject ils signals the plural.

items.fr: Je prends deux oeufs pour l'omelette.
items.en: I take two eggs for the omelette.
items.notes: La omelette is not possible to pronounce, so it becomes l'omelette.

items.fr: Le pain sent bon dans la cuisine.
items.en: The bread smells good in the kitchen.
items.ipa: /lə pɛ̃ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ dɑ̃ la kɥizin/
items.notes: Pain, sent and bon all rely on nasal vowels that leave no separate letter to hear.

items.fr: Elle sert la soupe très chaude.
items.en: She serves the soup very hot.
items.notes: The t at the end of sert is silent, so it is easy to forget when spelling the verb.

items.fr: Il verse l'huile dans la poêle.
items.en: He pours the oil into the pan.
items.notes: La huile is never said, la elides to l' before this vowel sound.

items.fr: Je ne mange pas de fromage.
items.notes: The mute e in je and ne is barely heard, so both words are easy to run together when writing.

items.fr: Elle achète du beurre frais pour la tarte.
items.en: She buys fresh butter for the pie.
items.ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt dy bœʁ fʁɛ puʁ la taʁt/
items.notes: Achète needs a grave accent on the e to keep the open sound, unlike acheter.

items.fr: Nous buvons un jus de fruits ensemble.
items.en: We drink a fruit juice together.
items.ipa: /nu byvɔ̃ œ̃ ʒy də fʁɥi ɑ̃sɑ̃bl/
items.notes: Un and ensemble both carry nasal vowels with no separate consonant sound to spell.

items.fr: Les invités arrivent pour le déjeuner.
items.notes: Les invités is joined by a z liaison since invités starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Je range les assiettes dans le placard.
items.en: I put the plates away in the cupboard.
items.notes: Les assiettes links with a z sound from les before the vowel of assiettes.

items.fr: Elle choisit un gâteau au chocolat.
items.notes: Gâteau keeps its circumflex accent on the a, a silent spelling clue.

items.fr: Tu manges trop de bonbons aujourd'hui.
items.en: You are eating too many candies today.
items.notes: Aujourd'hui is itself a frozen elision of au jour de hui and must be written as one word with an apostrophe.

items.fr: Les voisins cuisinent un plat traditionnel pour la fête.
items.en: The neighbors are cooking a traditional dish for the celebration.
items.ipa: /le vwazɛ̃ kɥizin œ̃ pla tʁadisjɔnɛl puʁ la fɛt/
items.notes: Cuisinent sounds just like the singular cuisine, so only les voisins shows it is plural.

items.fr: Je bois un jus d'orange le matin.
items.en: I drink orange juice in the morning.
items.ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ lə matɛ̃/
items.notes: Un and matin both end in nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound.

items.fr: Elle a acheté des tomates au marché.
items.en: She bought tomatoes at the market.
items.ipa: /ɛl a aʃte de tɔmat o maʁʃe/
items.notes: The auxiliary a and the preposition à sound identical, only the accent marks the difference.

items.fr: Nous avons mangé une pizza délicieuse.
items.notes: Mangé, manger and mangez are all pronounced the same way, so grammar must decide the ending.

items.fr: Il va préparer le dîner ce soir.
items.en: He is going to prepare dinner tonight.
items.ipa: /il va pʁepaʁe lə dine sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The final r of the infinitive préparer is never pronounced.

items.fr: Nous allons faire les courses ce matin.
items.en: We are going to do the grocery shopping this morning.
items.notes: Nous allons links with a z liaison before the vowel of allons.

items.fr: Elle a mis la table avant le repas.
items.en: She set the table before the meal.
items.ipa: /ɛl a mi la tabl avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The past participle mis ends in a silent s that is often forgotten in dictation.

items.fr: Ils ont mangé toutes les crêpes.
items.notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so only context shows which one is meant.

items.fr: On a préparé un gâteau pour son anniversaire.
items.en: We made a cake for his birthday.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ a pʁepaʁe œ̃ gato puʁ sɔ̃n‿anivɛʁsɛʁ/
items.notes: On is easily confused with ont since both are pronounced the same nasal sound.

items.en: Where did you buy this cheese?
items.notes: Où, meaning where, and ou, meaning or, are pronounced identically, only the accent separates them.

items.fr: Tu vas éplucher les pommes de terre.
items.en: You are going to peel the potatoes.
items.ipa: /ty va eplyʃe le pɔm də tɛʁ/
items.notes: The final r of éplucher stays silent, as in every -er infinitive.

items.fr: Elle a fait cuire les pâtes dix minutes.
items.en: She cooked the pasta for ten minutes.
items.ipa: /ɛl a fɛ kɥiʁ le pat di minyt/
items.notes: The irregular past participle fait ends in a silent t.

items.fr: Nous avons goûté la sauce avant de la servir.
items.en: We tasted the sauce before serving it.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ gute la sos avɑ̃ də la sɛʁviʁ/
items.notes: Goûté still carries the circumflex accent from goûter, even in the past participle.

items.fr: Les enfants ont bu tout le jus d'orange.
items.en: The children drank all the orange juice.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɔ̃ by tu lə ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: Enfants liaises into ont with a hidden z sound that must still be written as two words.

items.fr: Elle va couper les carottes en rondelles.
items.en: She is going to cut the carrots into rounds.
items.ipa: /ɛl va kupe le kaʁɔt ɑ̃ ʁɔ̃dɛl/
items.notes: Like all -er infinitives, couper ends in a completely silent r.

items.fr: J'ai lavé la salade avant de la manger.
items.en: I washed the salad before eating it.
items.ipa: /ʒe lave la salad avɑ̃ də la mɑ̃ʒe/
items.notes: Lavé, laver and lavez all sound the same, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not by ear.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté des pommes et des poires.
items.notes: Avons acheté chains two liaisons in a row that are easy to miss in fast speech.

items.fr: Il a versé l'huile dans la poêle chaude.
items.en: He poured the oil into the hot pan.
items.ipa: /il a vɛʁse lɥil dɑ̃ la pwal ʃod/
items.notes: La huile is unpronounceable, so it becomes l'huile before the vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle a préparé la soupe qu'elle a servie chaude.
items.en: She made the soup she served hot.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁepaʁe la sup kɛl a sɛʁvi ʃod/
items.notes: Servie is pronounced exactly like servi, but the silent added e agrees with the feminine soupe.

items.fr: On va manger dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are going to eat in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va mɑ̃ʒe dɑ̃ la kɥizin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: On here is easy to confuse with ont since both share the same nasal sound.

items.fr: Les invités sont arrivés avant le dîner.
items.notes: With être, arrivés adds a silent s to agree with the plural invités.

items.fr: Elle a coupé les légumes qu'elle a lavés ce matin.
items.en: She cut the vegetables she washed this morning.
items.ipa: /ɛl a kupe le legym kɛl a lave sə matɛ̃/
items.notes: Lavés sounds identical to lavé, but the silent s agrees with the plural légumes.

items.fr: Il faut que nous mangions des légumes variés chaque jour.
items.en: We must eat varied vegetables every day.
items.ipa: /il fo kə nu mɑ̃ʒjɔ̃ de legym vaʁje ʃak ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before the ending -ions, -ger verbs like manger drop the extra e since the following i already softens the g.

items.fr: Je ne pense pas que ce plat soit trop épicé.
items.en: I do not think this dish is too spicy.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə pla swa tʁo epise/
items.notes: Ce, meaning this, and se, the reflexive pronoun, are pronounced exactly the same way.

items.fr: Ces épices viennent du marché, mais ses habitudes culinaires ont changé.
items.en: These spices come from the market, but her cooking habits have changed.
items.ipa: /sez‿episɛ vjɛn dy maʁʃe mɛ sez‿abityd kylinɛʁ ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe/
items.notes: Ces and ses sound completely identical, so only grammar tells them apart.

items.fr: C'est la recette que ma grand-mère préférait.
items.en: This is the recipe my grandmother preferred.
items.ipa: /sɛ la ʁəsɛt kə ma gʁɑ̃mɛʁ pʁefeʁɛ/
items.notes: C'est sounds the same as ces and ses, so the apostrophe is the only visual clue.

items.fr: Quel plat préfères-tu pour le dîner de ce soir?
items.en: Which dish do you prefer for dinner tonight?
items.ipa: /kɛl pla pʁefɛʁ ty puʁ lə dine də sə swaʁ/
items.notes: Quel and quelle sound identical, so the ending must match the noun's gender in writing.

items.fr: Quelle sauce accompagne le mieux ce poisson grillé?
items.en: Which sauce goes best with this grilled fish?
items.ipa: /kɛl sos akɔ̃paɲ lə mjø sə pwasɔ̃ gʁije/
items.notes: Quelle sounds exactly like quel, so only the feminine noun sauce shows the correct spelling.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, elle continue à préparer le repas.
items.en: Although it is late, she keeps preparing the meal.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ ɛl kɔ̃tiny a pʁepaʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The subjunctive soit ends in a silent t that is easy to drop by mistake.

items.fr: Il faudrait que vous ajoutiez un peu plus de sel.
items.en: You should add a little more salt.
items.ipa: /il fodʁɛ kə vuz‿aʒutje œ̃ pø ply də sɛl/
items.notes: The ending -iez is pronounced yé, which is easy to confuse with the simpler -ez ending.

items.fr: Elle doute que ce dessert soit vraiment sans sucre.
items.en: She doubts this dessert is really sugar free.
items.ipa: /ɛl dut kə sə desɛʁ swa vʁɛmɑ̃ sɑ̃ sykʁ/
items.notes: Sans sounds identical to sang and cent, so only context fixes the spelling.

items.fr: Les invités, bien qu'ils aient déjà mangé, reprennent du gâteau.
items.en: The guests, although they already ate, take more cake.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite bjɛ̃ kilz‿ɛ deʒa mɑ̃ʒe ʁəpʁɛn dy gato/
items.notes: The subjunctive aient is pronounced just like est, with the whole ending staying silent.

items.fr: Ce cuisinier ne se souvient plus de la recette exacte.
items.en: This cook no longer remembers the exact recipe.
items.ipa: /sə kɥizinje nə sə suvjɛ̃ ply də la ʁəsɛt ɛgzakt/
items.notes: Ce and se appear together here and sound completely identical.

items.fr: Mes parents pensent que ces légumes sont meilleurs que les surgelés.
items.en: My parents think these vegetables are better than frozen ones.
items.ipa: /me paʁɑ̃ pɑ̃s kə se legym sɔ̃ mɛjœʁ kə le syʁʒəle/
items.notes: Ces is a homophone of ses and c'est, easily mixed up while writing quickly.

items.fr: Il semble que les enfants aient adoré le repas.
items.en: It seems the children loved the meal.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃z‿ɛ adɔʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The liaison before aient sounds just like the liaison before ont, so the two are easy to confuse when writing.

items.fr: Je voudrais que tu choisisses un dessert pour ce soir.
items.en: I would like you to choose a dessert for tonight.
items.ipa: /ʒə vudʁɛ kə ty ʃwazis œ̃ desɛʁ puʁ sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive choisisses is pronounced exactly like the indicative choisis, with the extra letters staying silent.

items.fr: Nous avons besoin d'un grand chef pour organiser ce banquet.
items.en: We need a great chef to organize this banquet.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ bəzwɛ̃ dœ̃ gʁɑ̃ ʃɛf puʁ ɔʁganize sə bɑ̃kɛ/
items.notes: De un is never said aloud, so it becomes d'un before the vowel.

items.fr: Ce dessert paraît trop sucré pour certains invités.
items.en: This dessert seems too sweet for some guests.
items.ipa: /sə desɛʁ paʁɛ tʁo sykʁe puʁ sɛʁtɛ̃z‿ɛ̃vite/
items.notes: Certains and invités both carry nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound before the liaison.

items.fr: Les grands chefs insistent pour que les ingrédients soient frais.
items.en: Great chefs insist that the ingredients be fresh.
items.ipa: /le gʁɑ̃ ʃɛfz‿ɛ̃sist puʁ kə lez‿ɛ̃gʁedjɑ̃ swat fʁɛ/
items.notes: The liaison after plural chefs is easy to mistake for the sound of a singular chef alone.

items.fr: Elle a l'habitude de goûter chaque plat avant qu'il ne soit servi.
items.en: She usually tastes every dish before it is served.
items.ipa: /ɛl a labityd də gute ʃak pla avɑ̃ kil nə swa sɛʁvi/
items.notes: La habitude cannot be pronounced, so it elides to l'habitude.

items.fr: Ses amis pensent que ce restaurant mérite trois étoiles.
items.en: Her friends think this restaurant deserves three stars.
items.ipa: /sez‿ami pɑ̃s kə sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ meʁit tʁwaz‿etwal/
items.notes: Ses sounds the same as ce and c'est, so only grammar reveals the right spelling.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux que nous réservions une table avant huit heures.
items.en: It is better that we reserve a table before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: /il vo mjø kə nu ʁezɛʁvjɔ̃ yn tabl avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ/
items.notes: The t of huit is silent alone but reappears in liaison before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: C'est étonnant que ces enfants aiment autant les épinards.
items.en: It is surprising that these children like spinach so much.
items.notes: C'est and ces are pronounced the same way, distinguishable only by their spelling and role.

items.fr: Quelles épices utilises-tu pour ce curry maison?
items.en: Which spices do you use for this homemade curry?
items.ipa: /kɛlz‿episɛ ytiliz ty puʁ sə kyʁi mɛzɔ̃/
items.notes: Quelles épices links with a z liaison that must still be spelled as two separate words.

items.fr: Bien que ce gâteau soit simple, il plaît à tout le monde.
items.en: Although this cake is simple, everyone likes it.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə gato swa sɛ̃pl il plɛ a tu lə mɔ̃d/
items.notes: Plaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent spelling detail carried over from plaire.

items.fr: Nous doutons que ses économies suffisent pour ce restaurant étoilé.
items.en: We doubt her savings are enough for this starred restaurant.
items.ipa: /nu dutɔ̃ kə sez‿ekɔnɔmi syfiz puʁ sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ etwale/
items.notes: Ses is a classic homophone trap, sounding identical to ce and c'est.
The final t in "vingt" is silent alone but is pronounced here before "ans".
"Quinze" and "ans" use two different nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling either one.
The final e in "quatre" is always silent, don't add an extra syllable when writing it.
"À" (preposition, with accent) sounds like "a" (verb avoir) but they are spelled differently.

items.fr: Le magasin ferme à dix-neuf heures.
items.en: The store closes at seven PM.
items.notes: "Neuf" changes its final sound from f to v before "heures".

items.fr: Le bus arrive à sept heures dix.
items.ipa: lə bys a.ʁiv a sɛ.tœʁ dis
items.notes: The p in "sept" is always silent, in every position, not just here.
The "an" sound in "quarante" is a nasal vowel, don't pronounce the r and n separately.
"Trente" carries a nasal vowel in its first syllable, spelled en but sounding like an.

items.en: We are leaving in ten minutes.
items.notes: Unlike in "dix heures", the x of "dix" stays silent here because "minutes" starts with a consonant.

items.en: My sister is sixteen years old.
items.notes: "Ans" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it when transcribing by ear.

items.en: We eat lunch right at noon.
items.notes: "Mangeons" keeps an extra e to preserve the soft j sound before the ending "ons".

items.fr: Nous sommes arrivés le premier septembre.
items.notes: Only "le premier" uses the ordinal for dates, every other day uses a plain number like le deux, le trois.

items.fr: Elle est née le deux mars.
items.en: She was born on March second.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ne lə dø maʁs
items.notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Ils sont partis le trois avril.
items.notes: "Partis" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

items.fr: Nous avons réservé une table pour huit heures.
items.en: We booked a table for eight o'clock.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl puʁ ɥi.tœʁ
items.notes: "Huit" liaises to a t sound before "heures" even though that t is silent on its own.

items.fr: Le cours a commencé à neuf heures pile.
items.en: The class started at nine o'clock sharp.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ a kɔ.mɑ̃.se a nœ.vœʁ pil
items.notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Elle va arriver à dix heures demain.
items.en: She is going to arrive at ten o'clock tomorrow.
items.ipa: ɛl va a.ʁi.ve a di.zœʁ də.mɛ̃
items.notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: Nous allons partir dans deux jours.
items.en: We are going to leave in two days.
items.notes: "Dans" is pronounced with a single nasal vowel, not a separate n sound.

items.fr: Ils ont fini leurs devoirs avant minuit.
items.en: They finished their homework before midnight.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ fi.ni lœʁ də.vwaʁ a.vɑ̃ mi.nɥi
items.notes: "Ont" (they have) sounds identical to "on" (one, we), context tells you which to write.

items.fr: On a mangé à midi et demi.
items.en: We ate at half past noon.
items.ipa: ɔ̃.n‿a mɑ̃.ʒe a mi.di e də.mi
items.notes: "Demi" stays masculine after "midi", it only becomes "demie" after a feminine noun like heure.

items.fr: Elle a eu vingt ans le mois dernier.
items.ipa: ɛl a y vɛ̃.tɑ̃ lə mwa dɛʁ.nje
items.notes: The silent t of "vingt" reappears here through liaison with "ans".

items.fr: Nous avons rendez-vous chez le médecin à quatorze heures.
items.en: We have an appointment at the doctor's at two PM.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʃe lə med.sɛ̃ a ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ
items.notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

items.fr: Le magasin a fermé à dix-neuf heures hier soir.
items.en: The store closed at seven PM last night.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ a fɛʁ.me a diz.nœ.vœʁ jɛʁ swaʁ
items.notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Je vais commencer mon nouveau travail le premier juin.
items.en: I am going to start my new job on June first.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ kɔ.mɑ̃.se mɔ̃ nu.vo tʁa.vaj lə pʁə.mje ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: Dates use the ordinal only for the first of the month, all later days use plain numbers.

items.fr: Nous avons déménagé le quinze octobre.
items.notes: "Quinze" holds a nasal vowel sound in its first syllable, not a plain i.

items.fr: Elle est arrivée en retard à la réunion.
items.en: She arrived late to the meeting.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
items.notes: "Arrivée" agrees with the feminine "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Ils vont se marier le vingt et un juin.
items.en: They are going to get married on June twenty-first.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ sə ma.ʁje lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: In compound numbers like vingt et un, the t of vingt is always pronounced, unlike the usual rule that et blocks liaison.

items.fr: Nous sommes nés la même année.
items.en: We were born in the same year.
items.ipa: nu sɔm ne la mɛm a.ne
items.notes: "Nés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "nous".

items.fr: Le train est parti à seize heures trente.
items.ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ ɛ paʁ.ti a sɛ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: With être, the past participle "parti" agrees with the masculine singular subject "le train", no extra ending.

items.fr: Elle a réservé son billet pour le douze mai.
items.en: She booked her ticket for May twelfth.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁe.zɛʁ.ve sɔ̃ bi.jɛ puʁ lə duz mɛ
items.notes: "Son" ends in a nasal vowel, listen closely before spelling it.

items.fr: Nous avons attendu le bus pendant vingt minutes.
items.en: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy lə bys pɑ̃.dɑ̃ vɛ̃ mi.nyt
items.notes: The t of "vingt" stays silent here since "minutes" starts with a consonant.

items.fr: Ils sont rentrés chez eux avant minuit.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.tʁe ʃe zø a.vɑ̃ mi.nɥi
items.notes: "Rentrés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

items.fr: Le film va commencer dans dix minutes.
items.en: The movie is going to start in ten minutes.
items.ipa: lə film va kɔ.mɑ̃.se dɑ̃ di mi.nyt
items.notes: The x of "dix" stays silent here because "minutes" begins with a consonant.

items.fr: Elle a fêté son anniversaire le sept mars.
items.en: She celebrated her birthday on March seventh.
items.ipa: ɛl a fe.te sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ lə sɛt maʁs
items.notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "anniversaire", producing an extra n sound.

items.fr: Nous allons voyager la semaine prochaine.
items.en: We are going to travel next week.
items.notes: The feminine "prochaine" loses the nasal sound of "prochain" because the final e opens the vowel.

items.fr: Le magasin ouvre à dix heures du lundi au vendredi.
items.en: The store opens at ten o'clock Monday through Friday.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ u.vʁ a di.zœʁ dy lœ̃.di o vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: Elle est partie en vacances le vingt-cinq juillet.
items.en: She left on vacation on July twenty-fifth.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ paʁ.ti ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s lə vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k ʒɥi.jɛ
items.notes: "Partie" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons un examen le trente novembre.
items.en: We have an exam on November thirtieth.
items.notes: "Novembre" carries a nasal vowel right after the v, don't skip it when spelling.

items.fr: Ils ont raté le train de sept heures.
items.en: They missed the seven o'clock train.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ ʁa.te lə tʁɛ̃ də sɛ.tœʁ
items.notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Elle va fêter ses dix-huit ans samedi prochain.
items.en: She is going to celebrate her eighteenth birthday next Saturday.
items.ipa: ɛl va fɛ.te se diz.ɥi.tɑ̃ sam.di pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: The silent t of "huit" is pronounced here because it liaises with "ans".

items.fr: Nous sommes sortis vers vingt et une heures.
items.en: We went out around nine PM.
items.ipa: nu sɔm sɔʁ.ti vɛʁ vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ
items.notes: "Heure" is feminine, so vingt et une heures uses "une", not "un".

items.fr: Le professeur a donné les résultats le quatre juin.
items.en: The teacher gave the results on June fourth.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a dɔ.ne le ʁe.zyl.ta lə katʁ ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: Both the final s and t of "résultats" stay silent in normal speech.

items.fr: Nous avons déjà réservé nos billets pour le seize décembre.
items.en: We have already booked our tickets for December sixteenth.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ de.ʒa ʁe.zɛʁ.ve no bi.jɛ puʁ lə sɛz de.sɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: "Décembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the s sound, easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Elle a répondu au message avant dix-huit heures.
items.en: She replied to the message before six PM.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁe.pɔ̃.dy o me.saʒ a.vɑ̃ diz.ɥi.tœʁ
items.notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Ils vont célébrer leur anniversaire de mariage le premier octobre.
items.en: They are going to celebrate their wedding anniversary on October first.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ də ma.ʁjaʒ lə pʁə.mje ɔk.tɔbʁ
items.notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal "premier", not later dates.

items.fr: Nous avons commencé les cours à huit heures et quart.
items.en: We started classes at a quarter past eight.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.se le kuʁ a ɥi.tœʁ e kaʁ
items.notes: The t of "huit" is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Elle est née un vingt-neuf février.
items.en: She was born on a February twenty-ninth.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ne œ̃ vɛ̃t.nœf fe.vʁje
items.notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Le vol va décoller à minuit trente.
items.en: The flight is going to take off at 12:30 AM.
items.ipa: lə vɔl va de.kɔ.le a mi.nɥi tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: "Trente" carries a nasal vowel in its first syllable, spelled en but sounding like an.

items.fr: Nous avons visité le musée le lendemain matin.
items.en: We visited the museum the next morning.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te lə my.ze lə lɑ̃d.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "Lendemain" and "matin" both end in nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Ils sont revenus deux jours plus tard.
items.en: They came back two days later.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁə.və.ny dø ʒuʁ ply taʁ
items.notes: The final d in "tard" is always silent in normal speech.

items.fr: Elle va passer son examen le vingt-trois mai.
items.en: She is going to take her exam on May twenty-third.
items.ipa: ɛl va pa.se sɔ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ lə vɛ̃t.tʁwa mɛ
items.notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "examen", producing an extra n sound.

items.fr: Nous avons attendu jusqu'à onze heures du soir.
items.en: We waited until eleven at night.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy ʒys.ka ɔ̃z œʁ dy swaʁ
items.notes: "Onze" is built on a single nasal vowel sound, not two separate syllables.

items.fr: Le magasin a ouvert ses portes à dix heures pile.
items.en: The store opened its doors right at ten o'clock.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ a u.vɛʁ se pɔʁt a di.zœʁ pil
items.notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: Elle a oublié le rendez-vous de quatorze heures.
items.en: She forgot the two o'clock appointment.
items.ipa: ɛl a u.bli.je lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu də ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ
items.notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

items.fr: Nous allons dîner ensemble vendredi soir.
items.en: We are going to have dinner together on Friday evening.
items.notes: "Ensemble" and "vendredi" both open with nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling.

items.fr: Ils ont signé le contrat le neuf septembre.
items.en: They signed the contract on September ninth.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ si.ɲe lə kɔ̃.tʁa lə nœf sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: The final t in "contrat" is always silent in normal speech.

items.fr: Elle est née à sept heures du matin.
items.en: She was born at seven in the morning.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ne a sɛ.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Nous avons fini le projet avant la date limite.
items.en: We finished the project before the deadline.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ fi.ni lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ a.vɑ̃ la dat li.mit
items.notes: The final t in "projet" is always silent in normal speech.

items.fr: Le cours a été annulé le vingt-six avril.
items.en: The class was cancelled on April twenty-sixth.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ a e.te a.ny.le lə vɛ̃t.sis a.vʁil
items.notes: "Annulé" is spelled with a double n, a common slip when writing from dictation.

items.fr: Elle va commencer son nouveau poste le deux janvier.
items.en: She is going to start her new position on January second.
items.ipa: ɛl va kɔ.mɑ̃.se sɔ̃ nu.vo pɔst lə dø ʒɑ̃.vje
items.notes: "Janvier" opens with a nasal vowel, don't confuse it with a plain a sound.

items.fr: Nous sommes restés jusqu'à minuit et demi.
items.en: We stayed until half past midnight.
items.ipa: nu sɔm ʁɛs.te ʒys.ka mi.nɥi e də.mi
items.notes: "Restés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "nous".

items.fr: Ils vont arriver vers dix-sept heures trente.
items.en: They are going to arrive around 5:30 PM.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ a.ʁi.ve vɛʁ diz.sɛ.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Elle a pris rendez-vous pour le vingt et un mars.
items.en: She made an appointment for March twenty-first.
items.ipa: ɛl a pʁi ʁɑ̃.de.vu puʁ lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ maʁs
items.notes: In vingt et un, the t of vingt stays pronounced even though et normally blocks liaison.

items.fr: Nous avons célébré son anniversaire le treize juin.
items.en: We celebrated her birthday on June thirteenth.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ lə tʁɛz ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of "anniversaire", producing an extra n sound.

items.fr: Le musée ferme à dix-huit heures le dimanche.
items.en: The museum closes at six PM on Sundays.
items.ipa: lə my.ze fɛʁm a diz.ɥi.tœʁ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: "Dimanche" ends in a nasal vowel followed by che, don't add a silent n before the ch.

items.fr: Elle est arrivée avec une heure de retard.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve a.vɛk yn œʁ də ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: "Arrivée" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons pris le petit-déjeuner à sept heures et demie.
items.en: We had breakfast at half past seven.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi lə pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne a sɛ.tœʁ e də.mi
items.notes: The p in "sept" is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Ils ont déménagé le premier avril.
items.notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal "premier".

items.fr: Elle va se réveiller à six heures du matin.
items.en: She is going to wake up at six in the morning.
items.ipa: ɛl va sə ʁe.vɛ.je a si.zœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The x of "six" turns into a z sound before the vowel of "heures".

items.fr: Nous avons raté notre correspondance à onze heures.
items.en: We missed our connection at eleven o'clock.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ʁa.te nɔtʁ kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃.dɑ̃s a ɔ̃z œʁ
items.notes: "Correspondance" and "onze" both rely on nasal vowels, listen closely before spelling.

items.fr: Le bébé est né à minuit pile.
items.en: The baby was born right at midnight.
items.ipa: lə be.be ɛ ne a mi.nɥi pil
items.notes: "Né" stays masculine to agree with "le bébé", no extra silent e is added.

items.fr: Elle a terminé ses études le trente juin.
items.en: She finished her studies on June thirtieth.
items.ipa: ɛl a tɛʁ.mi.ne se.z‿e.tyd lə tʁɑ̃t ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: "Trente" carries a nasal vowel spelled en but sounding like an.

items.fr: Nous allons nous retrouver à midi devant la gare.
items.en: We are going to meet up at noon in front of the station.
items.ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ nu ʁə.tʁu.ve a mi.di də.vɑ̃ la gaʁ
items.notes: "Devant" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it.

items.fr: Ils sont nés le même jour, à une heure d'intervalle.
items.en: They were born on the same day, an hour apart.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃ ne lə mɛm ʒuʁ a yn œʁ dɛ̃.tɛʁ.val
items.notes: "Nés" takes a silent final s to agree with the plural subject "ils".

items.fr: Elle a acheté son billet de train pour le dix-neuf mai.
items.en: She bought her train ticket for May nineteenth.
items.ipa: ɛl a a.ʃə.te sɔ̃ bi.jɛ də tʁɛ̃ puʁ lə diz.nœf mɛ
items.notes: The final t in "billet" is always silent in normal speech.

items.fr: Nous avons discuté jusqu'à vingt-trois heures.
items.notes: The x of trois liaises into a z sound right before heures.

items.fr: Le magasin est resté fermé pendant deux semaines.
items.en: The store stayed closed for two weeks.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɛ ʁɛs.te fɛʁ.me pɑ̃.dɑ̃ dø sə.mɛn
items.notes: "Pendant" is pronounced with a single nasal vowel repeated twice, not a separate n sound.

items.fr: Elle va démissionner à la fin du mois.
items.en: She is going to resign at the end of the month.
items.ipa: ɛl va de.mi.sjɔ.ne a la fɛ̃ dy mwa
items.notes: "Fin" ends in a nasal vowel, don't add a written n sound after it.

items.fr: Nous avons eu notre premier cours le lundi vingt mars.
items.en: We had our first class on Monday, March twentieth.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ y nɔtʁ pʁə.mje kuʁ lə lœ̃.di vɛ̃ maʁs
items.notes: The t of "vingt" stays silent here because "mars" begins with a consonant.

items.fr: Ils ont eu vingt-cinq ans le même jour.
items.en: They turned twenty-five on the same day.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ y vɛ̃t.sɛ̃.k‿ɑ̃ lə mɛm ʒuʁ
items.notes: The q of "cinq" liaises into a k sound right before "ans".

items.fr: Elle est partie à l'aéroport à cinq heures du matin.
items.en: She left for the airport at five in the morning.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ paʁ.ti a la.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ a sɛ̃.kœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "Le" elides to "l'" before the vowel sound of "aéroport".

items.fr: Nous avons pris nos vacances la dernière semaine d'août.
items.en: We took our vacation the last week of August.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi no va.kɑ̃s la dɛʁ.njɛʁ sə.mɛn dut
items.notes: "De" elides to "d'" before "août", where the initial vowel is pronounced.

items.fr: Le rendez-vous a été reporté au douze juillet.
items.en: The appointment was postponed to July twelfth.
items.ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu a e.te ʁə.pɔʁ.te o duz ʒɥi.jɛ
items.notes: The z in "rendez" is silent, the word ending sounds like "ay" not "ez".

items.fr: Elle a fêté ses trente ans en famille.
items.en: She celebrated her thirtieth birthday with family.
items.ipa: ɛl a fɛ.te se tʁɑ̃.tɑ̃ ɑ̃ fa.mij
items.notes: The t of "trente" liaises before the vowel of "ans".

items.fr: Nous allons fêter Noël le vingt-cinq décembre comme toujours.
items.en: We are going to celebrate Christmas on December twenty-fifth as always.
items.ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ fɛ.te nɔ.ɛl lə vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k de.sɑ̃bʁ kɔm tu.ʒuʁ
items.notes: "Décembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the s sound.

items.fr: Ils ont raté leur avion de dix heures et quart.
items.en: They missed their ten fifteen flight.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ ʁa.te lœʁ a.vjɔ̃ də di.zœʁ e kaʁ
items.notes: The x of "dix" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: Elle va rentrer chez elle vers vingt-deux heures.
items.en: She is going to go home around ten PM.
items.ipa: ɛl va ʁɑ̃.tʁe ʃe zɛl vɛʁ vɛ̃t.dø.zœʁ
items.notes: The x of "deux" liaises into a z sound right before "heures".

items.fr: Nous avons cours tous les jours sauf le mercredi.
items.en: We have class every day except Wednesday.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ kuʁ tu le ʒuʁ sof lə mɛʁ.kʁə.di
items.notes: The final s of "tous" is silent here because the next word starts with a consonant.

items.fr: Elle a envoyé le courrier avant midi.
items.en: She sent the mail before noon.
items.ipa: ɛl a ɑ̃.vwa.je lə ku.ʁje a.vɑ̃ mi.di
items.notes: "Envoyé" and "avant" both open with nasal vowels.

items.fr: Nous sommes partis en voyage le onze juillet.
items.en: We left on our trip on July eleventh.
items.ipa: nu sɔm paʁ.ti ɑ̃ vwa.jaʒ lə ɔ̃z ʒɥi.jɛ
items.notes: "Onze" is built on a single nasal vowel sound, not two separate syllables.

items.fr: Ils vont célébrer leurs retrouvailles le trente et un décembre.
items.en: They are going to celebrate their reunion on December thirty-first.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ ʁə.tʁu.vaj lə tʁɑ̃.t‿e œ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: The t of trente stays pronounced in this compound number despite et normally blocking liaison.

items.fr: Elle a pris sa retraite à soixante ans.
items.en: She retired at sixty years old.
items.ipa: ɛl a pʁi sa ʁə.tʁɛt a swa.sɑ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: The final t of "soixante" liaises before the vowel of "ans".

items.fr: Nous avons un cours supplémentaire le mardi après-midi.
items.en: We have an extra class on Tuesday afternoon.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃.z‿œ̃ kuʁ sy.ple.mɑ̃.tɛʁ lə maʁ.di a.pʁɛ mi.di
items.notes: "Supplémentaire" carries a nasal vowel in its middle syllable.

items.fr: Elle est née exactement à minuit.
items.en: She was born exactly at midnight.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ne ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ a mi.nɥi
items.notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject "elle", adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons quitté la maison à sept heures moins le quart.
items.en: We left the house at a quarter to seven.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ ki.te la mɛ.zɔ̃ a sɛ.tœʁ mwɛ̃ lə kaʁ
items.notes: The p in sept is silent, and its t liaises before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: Ils ont célébré leur mariage le quatorze février.
items.en: They celebrated their wedding on February fourteenth.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ se.le.bʁe lœʁ ma.ʁjaʒ lə ka.tɔʁz fe.vʁje
items.notes: "Célébré" repeats the accent é three times, easy to drop one when writing quickly.

items.fr: Elle va avoir vingt-deux ans dans trois semaines.
items.en: She is going to turn twenty-two in three weeks.
items.ipa: ɛl va a.vwaʁ vɛ̃t.dø.z‿ɑ̃ dɑ̃ tʁwa sə.mɛn
items.notes: The x of deux liaises into a z sound right before ans.

items.fr: Nous avons noté la date du seize septembre.
items.en: We noted the date of September sixteenth.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ nɔ.te la dat dy sɛz sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: "Septembre" holds a nasal vowel right after the p sound.

items.fr: Le cours particulier commence à dix-huit heures trente.
items.en: The private lesson starts at 6:30 PM.
items.ipa: lə kuʁ paʁ.ti.ky.lje kɔ.mɑ̃s a diz.ɥi.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: The t of huit is silent alone but liaises before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: Elle a annoncé son départ pour le vingt-huit août.
items.en: She announced her departure for August twenty-eighth.
items.ipa: ɛl a a.nɔ̃.se sɔ̃ de.paʁ puʁ lə vɛ̃t.ɥi.tut
items.notes: "Août" starts with a vowel sound, so huit liaises directly into it.

items.fr: Nous sommes allés au cinéma vers vingt et une heures.
items.en: We went to the movies around nine PM.
items.ipa: nu sɔm.z‿a.le o si.ne.ma vɛʁ vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ
items.notes: "Heure" is feminine, so vingt et une heures uses une, not un.

items.fr: Ils ont fixé la réunion au cinq mai.
items.en: They set the meeting for May fifth.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ fik.se la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ o sɛ̃k mɛ
items.notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound that is easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Elle va prendre sa retraite le premier janvier prochain.
items.en: She is going to retire next January first.
items.ipa: ɛl va pʁɑ̃dʁ sa ʁə.tʁɛt lə pʁə.mje ʒɑ̃.vje pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal premier.

items.fr: Nous avons dîné ensemble le soir de son anniversaire.
items.en: We had dinner together on the evening of her birthday.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ di.ne ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl lə swaʁ də sɔ̃.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: "Son" liaises with the vowel start of anniversaire, producing an extra n sound.

items.fr: Elle est revenue de vacances le vingt et un août.
items.en: She came back from vacation on August twenty-first.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ʁə.və.ny də va.kɑ̃s lə vɛ̃.t‿e u.tut
items.notes: "Revenue" agrees with the feminine subject elle, adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté les billets pour le concert de neuf heures.
items.en: We bought the tickets for the nine o'clock concert.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.ʃə.te le bi.jɛ puʁ lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ də nœ.vœʁ
items.notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: Ils sont restés éveillés jusqu'à deux heures du matin.
items.en: They stayed awake until two in the morning.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁɛs.te e.vɛ.je ʒys.ka dø.zœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The x of deux liaises into a z sound right before heures.

items.fr: Elle a signé le bail à partir du premier mars.
items.en: She signed the lease starting March first.
items.ipa: ɛl a si.ɲe lə baj a paʁ.tiʁ dy pʁə.mje maʁs
items.notes: Only the first of the month takes the ordinal premier.

items.fr: Nous allons nous marier le vingt-neuf juin prochain.
items.en: We are going to get married next June twenty-ninth.
items.ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ nu ma.ʁje lə vɛ̃t.nœf ʒɥɛ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: "Prochain" ends in a nasal vowel that is easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Ils ont annulé le vol de treize heures.
items.en: They cancelled the one PM flight.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ a.ny.le lə vɔl də tʁɛ.zœʁ
items.notes: "Treize" already ends in a pronounced z, which links smoothly into heures.

items.fr: Elle va avoir un entretien le trois octobre.
items.en: She is going to have an interview on October third.
items.ipa: ɛl va a.vwaʁ œ̃.n‿ɑ̃.tʁə.tjɛ̃ lə tʁwa ɔk.tɔbʁ
items.notes: "Entretien" opens and closes with nasal vowels, easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Nous avons pris le dernier train de la soirée.
items.en: We took the last train of the evening.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ pʁi lə dɛʁ.nje tʁɛ̃ də la swa.ʁe
items.notes: "Dernier" and "train" both carry nasal vowels close together.

items.fr: Elle est née la même année que son frère.
items.en: She was born the same year as her brother.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ ne la mɛm a.ne kə sɔ̃ fʁɛʁ
items.notes: "Née" agrees with the feminine subject elle, adding a silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons noté que le cours commence à neuf heures dix.
items.en: We noted that the class starts at 9:10.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ nɔ.te kə lə kuʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s a nœ.vœʁ dis
items.notes: "Neuf" shifts its final sound to v before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: Ils vont partir en retraite à soixante-cinq ans.
items.en: They are going to retire at sixty-five.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ ʁə.tʁɛt a swa.sɑ̃t.sɛ̃.kɑ̃
items.notes: The q of cinq liaises into a k sound right before ans.

items.fr: Elle a payé le loyer avant le cinq du mois.
items.en: She paid the rent before the fifth of the month.
items.ipa: ɛl a pe.je lə lwa.je a.vɑ̃ lə sɛ̃k dy mwa
items.notes: "Cinq" holds a nasal vowel sound that is easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Nous avons attendu toute la matinée sans nouvelles.
items.en: We waited all morning without news.
items.ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy tut la ma.ti.ne sɑ̃ nu.vɛl
items.notes: "Matinée" and "sans" both rely on nasal vowels that are easy to under-spell.

items.fr: Le vol a atterri à vingt-trois heures cinquante.
items.ipa: lə vɔl a a.tɛ.ʁi a vɛ̃t.tʁwa.zœʁ sɛ̃.kɑ̃t
items.notes: The x of trois liaises into a z sound right before heures.

items.fr: Elle a commencé ses cours de piano à cinq ans.
items.en: She started her piano lessons at age five.
items.ipa: ɛl a kɔ.mɑ̃.se se kuʁ də pja.no a sɛ̃.kɑ̃
items.notes: The q of cinq liaises into a k sound right before ans.

items.fr: Nous allons célébrer nos dix ans de mariage le vingt avril.
items.en: We are going to celebrate our tenth wedding anniversary on April twentieth.
items.ipa: nu.za.lɔ̃ se.le.bʁe no di.z‿ɑ̃ də ma.ʁjaʒ lə vɛ̃.t‿a.vʁil
items.notes: The x of dix liaises into a z sound right before ans.

items.fr: Il faut que nous soyons à l'aéroport avant sept heures du matin.
items.en: We must be at the airport before seven in the morning.
items.ipa: il fo kə nu swa.jɔ̃ a l‿a.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ a.vɑ̃ sɛ.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The subjunctive form soyons is easy to misspell or confuse with the indicative sommes, so listen for the -oy- spelling.

items.fr: Le rendez-vous est prévu pour le vingt et un mars à quatorze heures trente.
items.en: The appointment is scheduled for March twenty-first at two thirty in the afternoon.
items.ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu ɛ pʁe.vy puʁ lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ maʁs a ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
items.notes: The liaison in vingt et un pronounces the normally silent t of vingt before et.

items.fr: Nous nous verrons dans deux semaines, le temps que tu finisses ton rapport.
items.en: We will see each other in two weeks, by the time you finish your report.
items.ipa: nu nu vɛ.ʁɔ̃ dɑ̃ dø sə.mɛn lə tɑ̃ kə ty fi.nis tɔ̃ ʁa.pɔʁ
items.notes: The subjunctive finisses ends in a silent -es that is easy to drop when writing from dictation.

items.fr: C'est à neuf heures précises que la réunion commence.
items.en: It is at nine o'clock sharp that the meeting begins.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿a nœ.vœʁ pʁe.siz kə la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s
items.notes: Do not confuse c'est with ces or ses; only the elided form c'est fits this sentence.

items.fr: Ces dates ne conviennent à personne, il faudra les changer.
items.en: These dates do not suit anyone, they will have to be changed.
items.ipa: se dat nə kɔ̃.vjɛn a pɛʁ.sɔn il fo.dʁa le ʃɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: The demonstrative ces sounds identical to ses and c'est, so context alone decides the spelling.

items.fr: Quelle heure est-il exactement quand le train part de la gare ?
items.en: What time is it exactly when the train leaves the station?
items.ipa: kɛ.lœʁ ɛ.til ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ kɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃ paʁ də la ɡaʁ
items.notes: Quelle carries a silent final e that only surfaces through the liaison with heure, unlike the masculine quel.

items.fr: Il y a trois ans, nous avons déménagé à Lyon au mois de juin.
items.en: Three years ago, we moved to Lyon in the month of June.
items.ipa: il i a tʁwa.z‿ɑ̃ nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe a ljɔ̃ o mwa də ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: The liaison between trois and ans produces a z sound that must not be written into the word ans itself.

items.fr: Le magasin ferme ses portes à dix-huit heures trente les jours de semaine.
items.en: The store closes its doors at six thirty in the evening on weekdays.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ fɛʁm se pɔʁt a di.zɥi.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t le ʒuʁ də sə.mɛn
items.notes: Ses here is the possessive adjective and sounds exactly like ces and c'est, so spelling depends on meaning.

items.fr: D'ici la fin du mois, il faut que le projet soit terminé.
items.en: By the end of the month, the project needs to be finished.
items.ipa: di.si la fɛ̃ dy mwa il fo kə lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ swa tɛʁ.mi.ne
items.notes: The subjunctive soit is a homophone of soi and soie, so only the verbal context confirms the spelling.

items.fr: Se lever à cinq heures du matin devient difficile en hiver.
items.en: Getting up at five in the morning becomes difficult in winter.
items.ipa: sə lə.ve a sɛ̃.kœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃ də.vjɛ̃ di.fi.sil ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ
items.notes: The reflexive pronoun se before a verb is often confused in dictation with the conjunction ce.

items.fr: Ses horaires de travail changent chaque semaine selon le planning.
items.en: Her work hours change every week depending on the schedule.
items.ipa: se.z‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ də tʁa.vaj ʃɑ̃ʒ ʃak sə.mɛn sə.lɔ̃ lə pla.niŋ
items.notes: The possessive ses liaises with the following vowel of horaires, producing a z sound that signals the plural.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit déjà minuit, elle continue de travailler sur son mémoire.
items.en: Even though it is already midnight, she continues working on her thesis.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kil swa de.ʒa mi.nɥi ɛl kɔ̃.ti.ny də tʁa.va.je syʁ sɔ̃ me.mwaʁ
items.notes: After bien que, the verb must take the subjunctive soit, not the indicative est.

items.fr: Le concert commence à vingt heures, mais les portes ouvrent une heure avant.
items.en: The concert starts at eight in the evening, but the doors open an hour before.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s a vɛ̃.tœʁ mɛ le pɔʁt uvʁ yn œʁ a.vɑ̃
items.notes: The t of vingt is silent alone but resurfaces in liaison before heures, unlike in vingt et un.

items.fr: Nous attendons depuis longtemps que la date soit enfin fixée.
items.en: We have been waiting a long time for the date to finally be set.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.tɑ̃.dɔ̃ də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃ kə la dat swa ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fik.se
items.notes: The past participle fixée takes a silent final e to agree with the feminine noun date.

items.fr: L'examen aura lieu le premier juillet, à huit heures du matin.
items.en: The exam will take place on the first of July, at eight in the morning.
items.ipa: lɛg.za.mɛ̃ o.ʁa ljø lə pʁə.mje ʒɥi.jɛ a ɥi.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: The h of huit is mute, so the liaison with the article and with heures passes right through it.

items.fr: Il est essentiel que vous arriviez à l'heure pour l'entretien.
items.en: It is essential that you arrive on time for the interview.
